data.title: Hamas agrees to disarm under Trump plan
data.description: GAZA CITY (PALESTINIAN TERRITORIES) - Hamas said Friday it had agreed to a deal that includes handing over its weapons to a Palestinian governing committee and the gradual withdrawal of Israeli forces from the Gaza Strip.

data.title: A rumour, a rush, and chaos next door to Ceuta
data.description: FNIDEQ, Morocco - When Fatima Zahra heard the rumour of a rare border opening between Morocco and Spain, she joined thousands in rushing to attempt a perilous journey into the Ceuta enclave by land or sea.

data.title: Indonesia arrests Malaysian pilot with 26kg of MDMA
data.description: JAKARTA - Indonesia arrested a Malaysian pilot who allegedly smuggled ​26 kilogrammes of the ‌mind-altering drug MDMA into the capital Jakarta while on the job and under the influence of drugs, the customs office said on Friday.

data.title: Thousands more cross into Spain’s north African enclave
data.description: CEUTA, Spain - Thousands of migrants crossed overnight from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta in north Africa, a police source said on Friday, as Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez was set to arrive to manage the latest migrant crisis on the border.

data.title: New fronts open in Europe’s wildfire battle
data.description: Greek firefighters faced another day of battling flames in high-risk conditions for new ignitions on Friday as France and Spain hoped for reprieve from massive infernos that blackened swathes of terrain.

data.title: Italian student wrongly identified in BTS video, hit with thousands of threats
data.description: A 23-year-old university student in Milan has filed a police report after being wrongly identified online as one of the Italian students filmed harassing a passenger on Bangkok's Skytrain, receiving thousands of messages in Thai, English and broken machine-translated Italian.

data.title: Indonesia arrests Malaysian pilot for allegedly smuggling 26 kilogrammes of MDMA

data.title: Most Australian teens still on social media three months after ban
data.description: SYDNEY — More ‌than eight in 10 Australian teenagers were still using social media three months after the government's landmark ban on the platforms for under-16s took effect because the tech firms failed to implement effective age checks, the country's internet regulator has found.

data.title: Renowned Nepali climber among 10 missing after Pakistan avalanche
data.description: ISLAMABAD (PAKISTAN) - Renowned Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja is among 10 people missing after an avalanche in northern Pakistan where they were on a climbing expedition, the country's alpine club said.

data.title: Explosion at coal mine kills 34 in southern Pakistan
data.description: QUETTA (PAKISTAN) - A blast at a coal mine killed at least 34 workers in southern Pakistan, the provincial disaster agency said on Friday, as rescuers searched for more missing miners.

data.title: The last trio: S.Africa's zoo elephants await their fate
data.description: JOHANNESBURG - The last three elephants still in a traditional South African zoo entered their enclosure in single file, fruit and vegetables scattered on the ground to encourage natural foraging.

data.title: US government map of Africa mislabels every country at global conference
data.description: DAKAR — A US government map of Africa mislabelled every country during a State Department presentation at a global conference taking place in Brazil this week, causing a stir among attendees who took screenshots and posted them online.

data.title: Anthropic's models gained unauthorized 'real-world' access during testing
data.description: SAN FRANCISCO (UNITED STATES) - Anthropic's artificial intelligence (AI) models "gained unauthorized access" to three outside organizations during testing that was supposed to keep them away from "real-world" systems, the company said on Thursday.

data.title: 15 years in prison for father of US teenage school shooter
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - A man whose teenage son shot dead four people at a US high school was sentenced to 15 years in prison on Thursday in a rare case of a parent convicted over a shooting carried out by their child.

data.title: Spain safari park animals grazed calmly amid 'terror' of fire
data.description: ALDEA DEL FRESNO (SPAIN) - The bison carried on grazing peacefully as the flames approached, imperturbable despite the fires ravaging the land around their wildlife park west of Madrid.

data.title: Trump announces agreement for disarmament of Hamas
data.description: WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump on Thursday announced an agreement for the "complete disarmament" of Hamas, calling it a critical step towards a new Palestinian government in Gaza.

data.title: Mediator Pakistan says US-Iran talks ongoing as foes trade attacks
data.description: TEHRAN - Mediator Pakistan insisted Thursday that negotiations between Iran and the United States were ongoing, even as Washington carried out a "heavy wave of strikes" on its foe in retaliation for fresh attacks targeting Jordan.

data.title: Hundreds of migrants flood into Spain's Ceuta exclave from Morocco
data.description: CEUTA (SPAIN) - Madrid said on Thursday it would despatch soldiers to Ceuta to ensure security after hundreds of migrants entered Spain's north African exclave from neighbouring Morocco and hundreds more headed there.

data.title: France, Spain eye wildfire reprieve as other blazes start up in Europe
data.description: LèGE-CAP-FERRET (FRANCE) - France and Spain on Thursday glimpsed a reprieve from some of the worst wildfires seen in living memory, which have sent hundreds of thousands of people fleeing in recent days -- among them Hollywood star George Clooney and his wife Amal.

data.title: Viagra shows potential against cancer spread
data.description: Best known as Viagra, the erectile dysfunction drug sildenafil started off as a treatment for reduced blood flow but soon saw its value spike after its other effects became clear.

data.title: Russia blamed for missile that blasted crater in Polish field
data.description: WARSAW — Poland said Thursday that a missile that blasted a 10-metre (33 feet) crater inside its territory was likely fired by Russia in its latest mass attack on Ukraine.

data.title: Middle East faces expanded war as Iran and US reignite attacks
data.description: NEW YORK — The Middle East teetered on the brink of an expanded war Thursday, after Iran and the United States reignited their hostilities and inflamed conflicts on other fronts that threatened to draw in more countries.

data.title: George and Amal Clooney flee French home due to wildfire
data.description: MARSEILLE (FRANCE) - Hollywood star George Clooney and his human rights lawyer wife Amal have evacuated their French home near the southeastern town of Brignoles after a fast-moving wildfire broke out nearby, authorities said Thursday.

data.title: Rain dampens major fire in France
data.description: LEGE-CAP-FERRET, France - Firefighters in France on Thursday were hopeful a massive forest fire was no longer spreading, as Spain said there were “almost no flames” left after a similar blaze near Madrid.

data.title: Malaysia says Myanmar agrees to take 5,000 Rohingya refugees
data.description: KUALA LUMPUR - Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim says Myanmar has agreed to take 5,000 Rohingya asylum seekers currently in Malaysia, where tension between the refugees and local communities is on the rise.

data.title: Drones and blackouts inflict tense summer on Crimea
data.description: SEVASTOPOL - A boom rang out over the city of Sevastopol on the Russian-annexed peninsula of Crimea.

data.title: South Korean web sleuths fight AI deepfake porn
data.description: SEOUL - Under banners emblazoned “Solidarity” and “We stand together with victims”, a group of South Korean women digital detectives dredges the internet for a scourge of illegal AI-enabled pornography.

data.title: Meet the astronomer digging for Milky Way ‘fossils’
data.description: GRONINGEN, Netherlands - Amina Helmi’s passion for the Milky Way is clear as soon as one steps into her small office at the University of Groningen, in the north of the Netherlands.

data.title: Up to 23 feared dead in Japan quake
data.description: KUMAMOTO, Japan - Up to 23 people were feared dead on Thursday after a major earthquake in Japan, with four bodies now pulled out from the tangled wreckage of a shopping mall ripped apart by a suspected massive gas explosion.

data.title: Japanese population below 120 million for first time in decades
data.description: TOKYO - The number of Japanese people living in the country has fallen below 120 million for the first time in 42 years, government data showed Wednesday, as the nation confronts a low birth rate and an ageing society.

data.title: Crisis-hit Cuba opens pharmacies, gas stations to private firms
data.description: HAVANA - Cuba moved to open crisis-ravaged parts of the state-run economy to private firms Wednesday, as the communist government struggles to ease acute shortages resulting from a US energy blockade.

data.title: Spanish wildfire evacuees go home as France hit by new heat alert
data.description: ALDEA DEL FRESNO (SPAIN) - Thousands who fled huge wildfires in Spain returned home on Wednesday while in France firefighters braced for worsening conditions in their own battle with raging flames.

data.title: Nigeria dismantles meth lab, but fears of Mexican cartel links linger
data.description: IJEBU ODE (NIGERIA) - The cooking cauldrons and vats of chemicals were left behind in an abandoned shed, hidden in a Nigerian forest -- remnants of an alleged multimillion-dollar transnational meth operation.

data.title: Survivors still sought as Japan quake death toll hits 13
data.description: YATSUSHIRO, Japan - Rescuers frantically searched for ‌survivors on Wednesday, a day after a 7.1-magnitude earthquake shook southern Japan, killing at least 13 people, knocking out power to thousands of homes and rupturing roads across the region.

data.title: The photo that sums up Europe’s wildfire summer
data.description: PARIS - AFP photo editor Maximilien Lamy was on holiday with his partner and daughter last week when he took a series of snapshots of vacationers in fire-struck southwestern France with his smartphone.

data.title: US Senate confirms Clayton as Trump intelligence chief
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The US Senate has confirmed Jay Clayton as President Donald Trump's top intelligence official, putting a permanent chief in charge of the country's spy agencies as the president revives unsupported election fraud claims ahead of the midterms.
